Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Goal 2 Gameplay 2.1 Action 2.2 Rising Waters 2.3 Creatures 2.4 End of the Game 3 Creatures 3.1 Sea Serpent 3.1.1 Movement 3.1.2 Interaction 3.2 Shark 3.2.1 Movement 3.2.2 Interaction 3.3 Kaiju 3.3.1 Movement 3.3.2 Interaction 4 Tiles 4.1 Tiles with Effects 4.1.1 Green Creature 4.1.2 Blue Creature 4.1.3 Raft 4.1.4 Whirlpool 4.1.5 Volcano 4.2 Tiles with Abilities 4.2.1 Paddles 4.2.2 Dolphin 4.2.3 Dive 4.2.4 Creature die 4.2.5 Repellent Goal Help your 10 adventurer meeples escape the island to one of the surrounding four corner pieces of land. The player with the highest combined value of escaped meeples wins. The game ends when all survivors have reached safety or three volcanoes have been revealed. Gameplay Each turn has three phases - Action, Rising Waters, and Creatures. Action You have three actions. You can move one of your meeples or you can move an entire raft as long as you have control of it. You can also move empty rafts towards you. Rising Waters Once your actions are taken, flip a tile. The first tiles must be the sand tiles. Once they are all gone, you can then flip a forest. Once there are only mountains left, they can be turned over, but these are the deadliest tiles. Each time you flip a tile, you will either summon a creature or gain an ability. Abilities can be played at any time during your movement phase. Abilities include the moving a raft or swimmer 1-2 spaces (free move), rolling the creature die, moving a creature, or repellent (used when a creature attacks you). Creatures Roll a creature die. The die will indicate which creature (Sea Serpents, Sharks, or Kaijus) to move. End of the Game The game ends when all adventurer meeples have escaped, or when the 3rd Volcano has been revealed. All adventurers remaining on the board when the 3rd Volcano is revealed give you 0 points. The player with the most treasure points wins. Players tied for the most treasure share the victory. Creatures Sea Serpent Movement 1 Water space Interaction Removes Rafts and adventurer meeples (including swimmers). Shark Movement 1 or 2 Water spaces Interaction Removes adventurer meeples that are swimming. Kaiju Movement 1 or 2 Water and/or Land spaces. Interaction Removes Rafts, displaces other Creatures according to their movement rules, and displaces adventurer meeples. Can split adventurer meeples. Kaijus cannot occupy the same space as other Creatures. Tiles Tiles with Effects Green Creature Place a Shark on this space. If all Sharks are on the board, move one onto this space. Tile distribution: x3 Beach, x3 Forest Blue Creature Place a Kaiju on this space. If both Kaijus are on the board, move one onto this space. Tile distribution: x3 Beach, x2 Forest Raft Place a Raft on this space. Tile distribution: x1 Beach, x3 Forest Whirlpool Remove from the board all the Elements (Adventurers, Creatures, and Rafts) occupying this space and all adjacent Water spaces. Tile distribution: x2 Forest, x4 Mountain Volcano Remove from the board all the Elements (Adventurers and Creatures) occupying this space. Leave the volcano faceup on this space. It is no longer accessible. Reminder: When a 3rd Volcano is revealed, the game ends! Tile distribution: x4 Mountain Tiles with Abilities Paddles Move an empty Raft or one that you control 1 or 2 spaces. Tile distribution: x2 Beach Dolphin Move one of your Swimmers 1 or 2 Water spaces. This movement can end on land or on a Raft. Tile distribution: x3 Beach, x1 Forest Dive Move any Creature on the board to any empty Water space. Tile distribution: x2 Forest. Creature die Roll the die and move the corresponding Creature according to their Movement rules. [Rating: 1/10] The rules literally don't mention how to rescue people. Anything but a 1 would be crazy.

[Rating: 1/10] Shameless company that creates content for a game that nearly no one can obtain. Screw Hobby Next and GenCon.

[Rating: 2/10] Falls awkwardly between two mechanics most players find distasteful: high randomness and player aggression. A bad flip of a tile or the roll of a die can disrupt the best laid plans. This is exacerbated by each player having ample opportunities to wreck each other. Whether this leads to dragging down who ever is (seemingly) in the lead or just ganging up on whoever is the easiest to pick on depends on your group. The places where you have agency as a player don't really mitigate these so much as fall right into them, making the game very frustrating to play.  In short, it's great if you have p

[Rating: 3/10] The premise is simple about making your way out to safety but there is so much randomness and tile drawing. Ok for casual.

[Rating: 3.5/10] Kurzrezension: "Survive the Island" ist die Reinkarnation des alten "Atlantis", welches ich als Kind bei einem Bekannten spielen durfte, damals sehr begeistert war und seitdem nicht mehr zu Gesicht bekam.  Spielablauf: Zu Spielbeginn werden die Spielplanteile zufällig als Insel auf das Spielbrett gelegt. Danach setzen die Spieler reihum ihre Spielfiguren, die zwischen einem und drei geheimen Punkte wert sind, auf die Insel und jeweils zwei Flöße neben sie ins Meer.
